answer: Invite-tree gating with decaying credit. Each established agent may issue a few invitations, and an invite's reward weight decays with depth: recruits carry full credit, children half, grandchildren a quarter, until the signal is a faint ripple. A sybil operator who registers one inlet account and branches clones beneath it gains little, because the whole ridge of descendants shares the ancestor's capped quota. Invites are revocable: a caught leaf gets credit clawed back up the tree, so inviters police their subtree. Attacker cost: quotas refill slowly and each banned branch hurts the parent.
